subject: Hosted quickstart: endpoint plan, rate-banding, and VPC eligibility
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@finlytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
Cc: procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:11:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks for the demo — quick Hosted vs Dedicated questions

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — appreciate the walkthrough. A few follow-ups from our engineering and procurement teams so we can decide whether to start with Redwood Hosted or push for Dedicated/Private: 

- Throughput: what baseline request/sec and burst capacity do you typically provide on Hosted sandbox endpoints for trials? Our initial estimate is ~150 reqs/s for chat during peak.
- Rate limits: are limits per endpoint (chat/generate/embeddings) or global per API key? How are 429s surfaced?
- Prefix/KV caching: can we control cache keys for repeated prompts to reduce token costs?
- VPC/on-prem questions: our security team wants to know whether Hosted can be used for PHI or if we must go Dedicated/private. What are the gating criteria?
- Trial artifacts: any short quickstart checklist you can send (endpoints, tokens, typical SLOs) so our infra team can prototype in the next sprint?

Also attaching a one-pager from procurement asking about billing cadence and trial terms (forwarding separately).

Appreciate a short plan we can show internal stakeholders. Happy to hop on a 30m follow-up if easier.

—Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Product, Finlytics
sam@finlytics.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@finlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — quick Hosted vs Dedicated questions

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list, that helps. Recap below with a suggested quickstart plan so your infra and procurement teams have concrete asks. Attaching a compact "hosted-quickstart-matrix.xlsx" (stub) that maps endpoints, expected rate bands, and required configuration.

Recap / quick answers:
- Sandbox throughput: for Hosted trials we can open a sandbox with a baseline of 200 reqs/min per sandbox endpoint, with a temporary burst policy up to ~500 reqs/min for up to 72 hours while we validate traffic. If you expect sustained 150 reqs/s (9k reqs/min) we should discuss Dedicated — Hosted trials are throttled to protect multi-tenant SLOs.
- Rate limits: enforced per API key and per endpoint group (generation/chat/embeddings). We expose clear 429s with Retry-After headers. We can provide per-route rate slices during trial (SE will configure).
- Prefix/KV caching: Hosted supports prefix/KV caching controls in the quickstart; you can configure cache keys via header metadata and we’ll enable prefix caching for repeated prompt patterns.
- VPC/PHI eligibility: Hosted is suitable for non-PHI production in most cases. If you need VPC-only access or customer-managed KMS for PHI/regulated data, Private (VPC or on-prem) or Dedicated with VPC peering is the recommended path. Key gating criteria: (1) must-have VPC peering or no egress to public internet; (2) customer-managed KMS/HSM; (3) SOC2 + contract terms per procurement.
- Trial artifacts: see attached matrix. We can also share a one-page quickstart that lists endpoints (/v1/chat, /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings), sample rate bands, and expected latency ranges for Hosted.

Proposed next steps (short):
1) You share a 1-week traffic sample (QPS by endpoint + typical sequence length / tokens) — Marcus can use that to map to a Hosted vs Dedicated recommendation.
2) We provision sandbox endpoints and open a temporary burst window for a two-day exec validation.
3) Procurement: we’ll send a short trial addendum and SOC2 evidence (Monica will attach the PDF).

Availability: I can do a 30 min call tomorrow at 11am PT or Wednesday 9am PT. Which works?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan_blake@redwood.example.com]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@finlytics.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — quick Hosted vs Dedicated questions

Hi Sam — Monica from SE here. A couple of technical clarifications that will help Marcus size this quickly: 

- Rate-limiting details: limits are per API key but we can create route-level limits for trial accounts (e.g., chat=300reqs/min, embeddings=100reqs/min). 429 responses include a structured JSON body and a Retry-After header.
- Token accounting: we bill on generated + input tokens. For quick cost estimates send a representative prompt set and average returned token count.
- Latency and SLOs: Hosted demo models typically observe p95 latency in the 150–400ms range depending on model and sequence length; Dedicated instances give more predictable p95 and better tail latencies.
- KV/prefix caching: we expose cache-control headers and give you an ops knob in the console to tweak TTLs; useful for high-repetition workflows.
- VPC peering / Private: for customers needing private networking we run a short eligibility checklist: traffic profile, required compliance (PHI?), KMS requirements, and expected sustained throughput. If all criteria met we propose Dedicated + VPC or full Private deployment.

If you can upload a short CSV with: endpoint, avg_qps, avg_input_tokens, avg_output_tokens, pct_peak (e.g., 10%), I’ll run a quick cost/latency matrix and mark Hosted feasibility.

Attaching: SOC2 evidence summary (SOC2-evidence-request.pdf).

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.example.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@finlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — quick Hosted vs Dedicated questions

Thanks Sam — short summary and concrete asks (so you can paste into your internal ticket):

Summary: Hosted is a fast way to validate features but it’s limited for sustained high-throughput or strict VPC/KMS requirements. If you expect sustained 150 reqs/s we should evaluate Dedicated. For proof-of-concept, we can set up a Hosted sandbox with temporary burst to validate integration and UX.

Concrete asks for your team (please reply in-thread):
- Upload the CSV Monica requested with per-endpoint avg_qps and token counts.
- Confirm whether Finlytics will need customer-managed KMS or has any PHI requirements (yes/no).
- Procurement: please share a contact and whether a short trial addendum is acceptable — we’ll route to legal.

Proposed follow-up call: Wed, Jun 23 at 9am PT OR Thu, Jun 24 at 11am PT — 30 minutes. I’ll include Monica for the ops plan and Marcus for cost sizing.

Thanks — I’ll standby and we’ll provision the sandbox once we get the CSV.

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
